description: Fox's note looks like secret code to Robo: useless, unsafe, repaint. On Fox's Word Builder bench, green prefix blocks (un-, re-, pre-) click onto the front of blue base words and orange suffix blocks (-ful, -less, -er) click onto the end, each with a little demonstration of the new meaning, and the Fake Prefix Alarm catches words like uncle that only look like they have a prefix.

youtube.title: Word Builder Workshop! Prefixes and Suffixes for Kids | un, re, pre, ful, less, er | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Robo finds a note that looks like secret code: useless, unsafe, repaint! Fox shows him it's not code at all, just word parts. On the Word Builder bench, kids find the base word in the middle, add a prefix at the front (un- means not, re- means again, pre- means before) and a suffix at the end (-ful means full of, -less means without, -er means a person or thing that does something), and see each new meaning acted out: Dog repaints the door, a padlock unlocks, Robo carries a tower of cups carefully, then carelessly. Then the Fake Prefix Alarm: is uncle really un + cle? Take the part off and check that what's left is a real word.

For third graders (CCSS RF.3.3a, L.3.4b, L.3.4c).

Try at home: write un, re and pre on green paper, ful, less and er on orange paper, and base words like help, care, paint, fill and kind on blue paper. How many real words can you build? Act one out! Preheating an oven is a job for a grown-up.

do.text: Word Builder Workshop
Oh! There's a note on Fox's workshop door.
The old glue is useless.
The wet paint is unsafe to touch.
Please help me repaint the door.
Useless? Unsafe? Repaint? Fox is writing in secret code!
It's not code, Robo. They're word parts!
Big words are built from little parts. Let's build them and see!
This is my Word Builder bench.
Blue blocks are base words. A base word is a whole word by itself.
Safe. That's a base word.
Green blocks are prefixes. A prefix goes at the front of a base word.
prefix: at the front
Hold up your left hand. That's the front!
Un plus safe makes unsafe!
un + safe = unsafe
So what does unsafe mean? Think!
Unsafe means not safe. The prefix un- means not.
Like the wet paint! Not safe to touch.
Orange blocks are suffixes. A suffix goes at the end.
suffix: at the end
Hold up your right hand. That's the end!
My turn! I'll put -ful here.
Fulcare!
ful + care = fulcare?
Hmm. Fulcare is not a word. A suffix never goes at the front.
Care plus -ful makes careful. Careful means full of care.
Prefix at the front, suffix at the end, base word in the middle!

scenes.title: The prefix bench: un-, re-, pre-

do.text: Let's start with three prefixes. First, un-.
I'm happy. Now add un-.
Unhappy. Not happy.
Unkind means not kind.
unkind = not kind
Unfair means not fair.
unfair = not fair
Cheer up, Robo! Un- can also mean the opposite.
Lock. The padlock is locked shut.
Unlock is the opposite of lock.
Unsafe, unhappy, unlock. Un- means not, or the opposite.
un- = not, the opposite of
Hello! I'm Dog, the painter. I painted this door blue yesterday.
But it needs a new colour. Time to paint it again!
Re- plus paint makes repaint. Repaint means paint again.
re- = again
Now watch the glass. Robo pours the water out.
Empty! What word means fill it again?
Refill! Fill again.
I built a tower. Oops!
Time to rebuild. Build it again!
Repaint, refill, rebuild, reread. In these words, re- means again.
re- = again
Last prefix: pre-. Pre- means before.
pre- = before
We're baking cupcakes. Ovens are a job for a grown-up, like me.
First I heat the oven, before the cupcakes go in.
Pre- plus heat makes preheat. Heat before.
And a preview lets you see a movie before it comes out.
Fun fact! The word prefix has a prefix. Pre- plus fix: fixed on before.
pre + fix = prefix
And re- and pre- came from Latin, but un- comes from Old English!
Now the suffixes, at the end. Care plus -ful makes careful.
Robo, show us careful. Carry these cups.
careful = full of care
Slow and steady. Every cup stays up. I'm full of care!
Now swap the suffix. Care plus -less makes careless.
Careless means without care. Show us careless, Robo!
careless = without care
Oops! Soft landing on the rug. Nothing broke.
But that was careless. I'll be careful from now on.
Remember the old glue? Watch this paper.
It won't stick. Glue that is useful is full of use.
This glue is useless. Without use!
useless = without use
One more suffix: -er. It means a person or thing that does something.
-er = one who does
Paint plus -er makes painter. A painter is a person who paints. That's me!
Build plus -er makes builder. A builder is a person who builds. That's me!
And a mixer is a thing that mixes! -er can name things too.
mixer = a thing that mixes
Chant with me! Tap the beat on your knees!
Prefix at the front!
Suffix at the end!
Base word in the middle is your best friend!
Prefix at the front!
Suffix at the end!
Base word in the middle is your best friend!
un + help + ful
Re-?
Again!
-less?
Without!
-ful?
Full of!
That chant word had a prefix and a suffix. Start with the base: help.
Add -ful at the end. Helpful: full of help.
Now add un- at the front. Unhelpful!
Un, help, -ful. What does it mean? Peel it from the outside!
Helpful means full of help. Unhelpful means not helpful.
One base, two suffixes. Careful and careless are opposites!
This is my Fake Prefix Alarm. Some words only look like they have a prefix.
I know one! Uncle starts with un-. So uncle means not C, L, E!
Let's test it. Take un- off. What's left?
C, L, E is not a word! So uncle has no prefix. It's just a base word.
Real! Is that re- plus A, L?
A, L is not a word. Alarm! Real is just a base word.
Your turn. Pretty. Take pre- off. Is the leftover a word?
No! Pretty has no prefix. The alarm caught it!
Now I wrote a note in word parts. Can you decode it?
I will reread the book, be fearless on the slide,
preview the movie, and be a helpful builder.
First word: reread. What does it mean?
Re- means again. Reread means read again.
Next: fearless. What does it mean?
-less means without. Fearless means without fear.
Next: preview. What does it mean?
Pre- means before. Preview means to see before.
Next: helpful. What does it mean?
-ful means full of. Helpful means full of help.
Next: builder. What does it mean?
A builder is a person who builds.
One trick word! Is under un- plus D, E, R?
No! D, E, R is not a word. Under is a base word. Great decoding!
Quiz time! Five quick questions.
What does reread mean?
Read again!
What does fearless mean?
Without fear!
Which word means not fair?
Unfair!
What is the base word in preheat? And in helpful?
Heat and help!
Does uncle have the prefix un-?
No! C, L, E is not a word.
Here's the recap. The base word is in the middle.
Prefixes go at the front: un- means not, re- again, pre- before.
un- not · re- again · pre- before
Suffixes go at the end: full of, without, and one who does.
-ful full of · -less without · -er one who
And check that the leftover is a real word!
The door is finished. Wonderful work, everyone!
Wonderful: wonder plus -ful. Built, checked, beautiful!
